issue_context.title: Growatt Server - Incorrect Units Assigned
issue_context.body: ### The problem In the 'Growatt Server' integration, the units used for some of the sensors are incorrect. The total PV wattage is 0.46 kW which is correct, however the sensors for the two individual strings are assigned the unit 'W' rather than 'kW' resulting in a figure that is incompatible. Request to have the units corrected to display each PV string as 'kW' please! ### What is version of Home Assistant Core has the issue? 2021.6.0 ### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core? _No response_ ### What type of installation are you running? Home Assistant OS ### Integration causing the issue Growatt Server ### Link to integration documentation on our website https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/growatt_server/ ### Example YAML snippet _No response_ ### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us? _No response_ ### Additional information
comments:
Hi @headbouyJB thanks for the tag, would have never have seen this otherwise!
I'll compare against my own system tomorrow but I implemented the logic for the "hybrid/mixed" system and I'm confident it was accurate.
The fact you're seeing individual panel readings means that your system should be supported, otherwise you only get the totals.
All seems a bit weird...

Curiosity got the better of me so I had to take a look at it for myself!
It looks like the growatt API itself has changed from reporting this value in W is now reported in KW (this is the problem with a 3rd party application that we've reverse engineered a library against - it's subject to change without any warning).
I'm basing this on the code I wrote here: https://github.com/indykoning/PyPi_GrowattServer/blob/master/mix_example.py#L195-L200
You'll notice that on line 198 I divided the sum of the two PV wattages by 1000 in order to get the KW value before comparing it to the total value that the API reports.

I have all of my data from Growatt backed up in influxdb, so tomorrow I'll go back through my history in grafana and find the point that it changed - it would be good to pinpoint the date. 

Once I've done that I'll happily put a PR together to get this changed!

At least we've established that this is consistent across installations and isn't specific to just yourself!

Curiosity got the better of me again, just threw this together in Grafana:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10612068/122473706-21a10700-cfba-11eb-8bbd-ae7829208eb4.png)

The image shows readings for PV1 wattage over 7 days, the first 4 are in Watts (note the 'k' on the Y-Axis), the second three essentially vanish because they're in KW (I can assure you though, that when I hover over the data points they are still there, they're just so close to 0 they don't register on the graph)
Therefore, growatt changed the value on that part of the API from W to KW at around 00:00 (UK time) on 14th April.

Anyway, that's all good to know and hopefully restores your faith in the code that @indykoning and I have written - it was correct at one point :p

It's getting pretty late here in the UK, so the PR will have to wait until tomorrow, but I'll get this pushed in tomorrow and hopefully it'll be merged into Dev without too much hassle.

I'll need to also update my example on the Pypi library, but that won't affect this code, it's just for consistency.

Thanks @muppet3000 for getting onto this so quickly!
Started a new job so wasn't able to jump in as you were working through all that...
I never doubted your code for a minute!

Now who do I approach to work with for Growatt Hybrid Inverter scheduling? :-P

@headbouyJB no problem, have you had the chance to test it yet?

Funny you should mention inverter scheduling, would you believe it if I told you I'm actually working on this in the background at the minute?
I assume you mean something like "if the weather forecast is going to be cloudy tomorrow, then fill the batteries to 100% during my cheap charging rate overnight"?
If that's the case, that's what I'm working on, it's not going to be in HomeAssistant though (at least to start with). 
Rather than continuing the discussion here, drop me an email (address is on my GitHub page) and I'll fill you in.
